string.text: This is a standard .45 ACP (11.43x23mm) cartridge used in the Colt M1911, SIG Sauer P220, USP Compact, and Desert Eagle pistols. Renowned for its high accuracy and lethality, it has remained popular for over a century. A drawback of this caliber is its low muzzle velocity, which results from the heavy weight of the bullet combined with a relatively modest propellant charge.

This .45 ACP (11.43x23mm) cartridge features a lead expanding bullet known as Hydra-Shok that offers excellent stopping power and penetration. This is an enhanced-performance round designed for use with the Colt M1911, SIG Sauer P220, USP Compact, and Desert Eagle pistols.
Standard 12-gauge round filled with 6mm shot. Highly lethal at close range. Only suitable for use with smoothbore weapons - specifically the TOZ-34, the TOZ-66, the Maverick 88, and the SPAS-12.

A specialized 12-gauge round that's similiar to a slug, but more pointed. Its fins add stability, resulting in increased accuracy. The massive steel body of the bullet can penetrate any body armor. This round is used by 12-gauge shotguns - the TOZ-34, the TOZ-66, the Maverick 88, and the SPAS-12.

This heavy 12-gauge slug round is normally used for hunting big game, but is also good for other purposes. Instead of piercing, this hefty slug simply crushes through armor. This round is used by 12-gauge shotguns - the TOZ-34, the TOZ-66, the Maverick 88, and the SPAS-12.
An armor-piercing 5.45x39mm caliber cartridge for the AKS-74, AKS-74U, and RPK-74 assault rifles.

Standard 5.45x39mm caliber cartridge for the AKS-74, AKS-74U, and RPK-74 assault rifles. It provides better accuracy than the 7.62x39mm caliber rounds thanks to its reduced recoil and increased firing range.
An armor-piercing 5.56x45mm caliber cartridge for the L85, LR-300, SIG SG 550, G36, and FN-2000 assault rifles.

A standard issue NATO 5.56x45mm caliber cartridge for the L85, LR-300, SIG SG 550, G36, and FN-2000 assault rifles. It was specially designed for accurate automatic fire, and is widely known under its Belgian SS109 designation.

A model 1943 intermediate full-metal-jacket 7.62x39mm caliber cartridge for the AKMS and RPK assault rifles. Due to a long storage period, these rounds have significantly deteriorated, which leads to increased wear on the firearm.
An inexpensive-to-manufacture 7.62x54R caliber cartridge for the SVD and OTs-03 SVU sniper rifles.

A 7.62x54R 7N14 caliber cartridge for the SVD and OTs-03 SVU sniper rifles enhanced with elements of a gravitational artifact; manufactured by Cobalt. The cartridge’s lethality is significantly increased, though its use takes a heavy toll on the condition of the weapon.
A sniper armor-piercing (SAP) 7.62x54R cartridge for the SVD and OTs-03 SVU sniper rifles. It's intended for engaging armored targets at long ranges.
An armor-piercing 7.62x54R cartridge for SVD and OTs-03 SVU sniper rifles, designed for engaging heavily-armored targets.
Standard 9x18mm caliber cartridge for the PM, PB, Fort-12, and APS pistols, as well as the AEK-919K submachine gun. Features a simple core and a jacketed bullet. Weak armor-piercing capability.

An armor-piercing 9x18mm caliber cartridge for the PM, PB, Fort-12, and APS pistols, as well as the AEK-919K submachine gun. This is a high-power round featuring an expanding bullet with an armor-piercing core.

A 9x18mm caliber cartridge with enhanced ballistic characteristics, designed for the PM, PB, Fort-12, and APS pistols, as well as the AEK-919K submachine gun. Due to a higher initial bullet velocity, it is significantly more effective than the standard PM cartridge and possesses a more pronounced armor-piercing capability.

A standard 9x19mm caliber cartridge for the Browning HPSA, Walther P99, Beretta 92FS, and GSh-18 pistols, as well as the MP5 submachine gun. Features a full metal jacket (FMJ) bullet. Has limited armor-piercing capability.

A 9x19mm caliber cartridge with enhanced performance characteristics, designed for the Browning HPSA, Walther P99, Beretta 92FS, and GSh-18 pistols, as well as the MP5 submachine gun. This high-power round features an expanding bullet with an armor-piercing core.

An armor-piercing 9x39mm caliber cartridge designed for the OTs-12 "Tiss," OTs-14 "Groza," AS "Val," and VSS "Vintorez" firearms. Although it travels at a subsonic velocity, its specially designed bullet allows it to penetrate most types of body armor at ranges of up to 400 meters.

An inexpensive variant of the 9x39mm armor-piercing cartridge, designed for the OTs-12 "Tiss," OTs-14 "Groza," AS "Val," and VSS "Vintorez" firearms. Although it travels at a subsonic velocity, its specially designed bullet allows it to penetrate most types of body armor at ranges of up to 300 meters.

A 9x39mm caliber sniper cartridge designed for the OTs-12 "Tiss," OTs-14 "Groza," AS "Val," and VSS "Vintorez" firearms. It features a subsonic muzzle velocity, yet its heavy, specially designed bullet allows it to penetrate most types of body armor at ranges of up to 400 meters.
These gauss rifle magazines consist of both rounds and a battery using a capsulated fragment of an energy artifact as a power source. They are manufactured using high-tech equipment.
The M406 is a 40 mm grenade for the M203 underbarrel grenade launcher. It has a 5 meter kill zone, and it's also used by the integrated underbarrel grenade launcher of the FN-2000.
The OG-7B is a high explosive, tandem charge warhead grenade that's for the RPG-7V. It's devastating against mutants, stalkers, troops, and lightly armored vehicles.

The VOG-25 is a fragmentation grenade for the GP-25 "Kostyor" underbarrel grenade launcher. This grenade has an effective radius of five meters. The VOG-25 grenade is also used by the OTs-14 Groza's underbarrel grenade launcher and RG-6 revolving grenade launcher.

The VOG-25P is a improved fragmentation grenade for the GP-25 "Kostyor" underbarrel grenade launcher. This grenade has effective radius of five meters - but fefore detonation, the grenade jumps up to a height of about a meter, which increases its lethality. The VOG-25P grenade is also used by the OTs-14 Groza's underbarrel grenade launcher and RG-6 revolving grenade launcher.
A flashlight that has a modified bulb and voltage regulator, giving it better brightness. Quite useful at nighttime or in areas with little or no lighting

This specific G36 has been altered by spraying powder from a grounded up gravitational artifact onto the barrel, improving overall accuracy.
 Ammunition:
 standard 5.56x45mm SS109,
 armor-piercing 5.56x45mm AP.,
M209 grenade
An F-1 grenade that has been enhanced with a Gravi artifact. It draws in enemies after it detonates, and then propels them away, making this grenade considerably more dangerous.

A defensive hand grenade, with fragments capable of piercing medium-level body armor. The grenade has an effective range of 7 meters. Stalkers get F1 grenades from trading with the military bureaucrats, who write them off as having been used for fighting mutants.
An RGD-5 grenade that has been enhanced with a Gravi artifact. It draws in enemies after it detonates, and then propels them away, making this grenade considerably more dangerous.
An offensive hand grenade with a small effective range of 5 meters. These are often used by stalkers to "smoke out" mutants due to its relatively low cost.

An underbarrel grenade launcher for the AKMS assault rifle.
Ammunition:
VOG-25
VOG-25R

A single shot, front loaded, rifled underbarrel grenade launcher for assault rifles made in Warsaw Pact countries. The firing mechanism is self-cocking, with a manual safety catch and automatic shot prevention if incorrectly installed onto a rifle.
 
Ammunition:
VOG-25 grenade
VOG-25R grenade

A modified M203 grenade launcher that has been shortened by three inches, attached to weapons by means of a Picatinny rail. Thanks to a changed mount, this grenade launcher is widely used around the world.
 
Ammunition:
M406 grenade
This is an old Soviet-made optical scope for the AKMS assault rifle. It attaches to weapons by means of a Dovetail mount, which is standard for weapons used by former Warsaw Pact countries.
The PSO-1 is a very common Soviet-made optical scope. It attaches to weapons by means of a Dovetail mount, which is standard for weapons used by former Warsaw Pact countries.

A 4x fixed zoom scope produced primarily in Western countries. It attaches to weapons by means of the NATO-standardized Picatinny rail. Often used for accurate fire from small arms at medium to long range.

An effective silencer which can be modified on the go as required. The body of the silencer around the barrel contains a roll of fine brass mesh, while the front comprises a set of metal diaphragms with holes for the bullet to pass through. The set includes adaptors and sealants for most weapons. Normally used to thin out enemy ranks without drawing attention.

A Russian submachine gun chambered for the 9x18mm cartridge, developed in the 1990s for use by law enforcement special units and for the equipment of combat vehicle crews. It is fitted with an integrated suppressor.
 Ammunition:
 standard 9x18mm FMJ,
 armor-piercing 9x18mm JSP-AP, 
 improved 9x18mm +P+.

Kalashnikov rifles were developed in line with the military doctrine of the time—prioritizing maximum affordability, reliability, and simplicity—which came at the expense of some ease of use and firing accuracy. In the Zone, this weapon is used by the military and experienced stalkers. 
 Ammunition:
 standard 5.45x39mm FMJ,
 armor-piercing 5.45x39mm AP.

A variant of the AK-74 with an integrated higher-magnification sight, developed for the USSR Ministry of Defense competition aimed at creating an assault rifle with significantly improved accuracy and shot-grouping performance. Although the competition was won by the Nikonov designed assault rifle, small batches of the AKS-74 “Yenisei” continue to be produced on the account of special orders.
 Ammunition:
 standard 5.45x39mm FMJ,
 armor-piercing 5.45x39mm AP.

Modification of the AKM assault rifle with a folding metal rifle butt, a design similar to the AKS. Due to the poor accuracy, compared to more modern assault rifles, it's not the best tool for far shooting. 
AKMS used mainly among conscripts and stalkers who cannot afford a better weapon.
 Ammunition:
 standard 7.62x39mm.

The weight and size of the AKS-74U are similar to those of a submachine gun, but its operation mode and the ammunition it uses place it into the class of the assault rifles. Its advantages are its small dimensions very useful when fighting inside a building or in a thick forest and a relatively high piercing capabilities. Its main disadvantages are a limited accuracy range and quick overheating when firing bursts.
 Ammunition:
 standard 5.45x39mm FMJ,
 armor-piercing 5.45x39mm AP.

A variant of the AKS-74U featuring an integral suppressor, designed for special operations forces. Due to a number of design flaws, a search for a replacement began shortly after it entered service. 
The “Pikhta” and “Tiss” projects aimed to modernize the AKS-74UB; however, despite significant improvements, they failed to outperform alternatives such as the AS “Val”. Nevertheless, it continues to be produced in small batches on a special-order basis.
 Ammunition:
 standard 5.45x39mm FMJ,
 armor-piercing 5.45x39mm AP.

At first glance this looks like the legendary AKMSU, but turns out it is a work of an unknown, amateur gunsmith who cobbled it together using parts from an AKMS, an AKS-74U, and an OTs-14 “Groza”. One can only guess who created this "Frankenstein" and for what purpose. \n Ammunition:\n standard 7.62x39mm.

The Stechkin APS is a machine pistol developed during the late 1940s and early 1950s, and was officially adopted by the Soviet Armed Forces in 1951 alongside the Makarov PM. The APS is intended for arming officers taking direct part in combat operations, as well as for soldiers and sergeants of special units.
 Ammunition:
 standard 9x18mm FMJ,
 armor-piercing 9x18mm JSP-AP, 
 improved 9x18mm +P+.

Adopted by the American army and police, as well as many military and police units all over the world. It is also very popular among the criminals for its high-powered round and its high-capacity magazine.
 Ammunition:
 standard 9x19 mm FMJ,
 improved 9x19 mm JHP.

The primary feature that distinguishes this rare model from the widely used 92 series is its three-round burst firing mode, as well as a higher RPM, an enlarged 21-round magazine, and a heavier slide. 
It was taken out of production in 1993 following the emergence of more affordable submachine guns, such as the MP5. How such a rare specimen ended up in the Zone remains unknown. 
 Ammunition:
 standard 9x19mm Parabellum,
 improved 9x19mm JSP-AP.

A standard side-by-side hunting shotgun. Nothing remarkable about it. One of the most common types of weapons among beginners.
Ammunition:
12x70 Buckshot,
12x76mm Slug,
12x76mm Dart

The BM-16 shotgun belonging to the legendary Dark Stalker looks no different from the standard model, except for its remarkably light weight.
Ammunition:
12x70 Buckshot,
12x76mm Slug,
12x76mm Dart

An improved version of the classic Colt 1911 automatic pistol, which passed all the major armed conflicts of the 20th century with flying colors and entered the new millennium with confidence. Produced by dozens if not hundreds of arms manufacturers around the world in both standard and modified configurations. The weapon's only drawback, its mediocre magazine capacity, is largely compensated by the hard-hitting ammo it uses.
 Ammunition:
 standard .45 ACP,
 improved .45 ACP Hydra-Shok.

A real gun for real heroes. It is big, heavy and very destructive. It is not very popular in the Zone due to its price and size. After all, you don't go hunting for elephants every day!
 Ammunition:
 standard .45 ACP,
 improved .45 ACP Hydra-Shok.

This futuristic-looking weapon with a bullpup layout is actually a mass produced modular system, comprising a rifle grenade complex with a computerized fire control system and a 40-mm grenade launcher. Despite its bulky appearance, the weapon is highly ergonomic, easy to use and benefits from good reliability.
 Ammunition:
 standard 5.56x45mm SS109,
 armor-piercing 5.56x45mm AP.,
M209 grenade

A Ukranian-made pistol predominantly used by law enforcement organizations. Compared to the Makarov PM, the Fort-12 has better higher accuracy, better ergonomics and has a larger magazine. These pistols make it into the Zone in large numbers thanks to the sale of defective weapons, which suffer from technical flaws in early design models. Despite this, the pistol is in demand among stalkers thanks to its good combat characteristics.
 Ammunition:
 standard 9x18mm FMJ,
 armor-piercing 9x18mm JSP-AP, 
 improved 9x18mm +P+.

The G36 is a new addition to the Western-made assault rifle family, which differs significantly from previous models in the series built on an automatic foundation with a semi-open bolt assembly, this weapon is more like American automatic gas-operated assault rifles with a short-stroke gas piston system. These changes ensure that the rifle is a first-rate example of a modern weapon - lightweight, reliable and ergonomic.
 Ammunition:
 standard 5.56x45mm SS109,
 armor-piercing 5.56x45mm AP.

This gauss rifle is a highly accurate, technologically advanced weapon. It was developed in secret laboratories located inside the Zone. The weapon operates by accelerating bullets to extremely high speeds using a system of electromagnets, which provides incredible stopping power with virtually no recoil. The weapon is powered by using capsulated artifact fragments stored in the batteries.
 
Ammunition:
2mm gauss rounds

A gauss rifle that comes with a enlarged detachable magazine, having a larger capacity of rounds.
 
 Ammunition:
2mm gauss rounds

This assault rifle combined with a grenade launcher, which is similar to the AK series, was specifically developed for rapid response units. The main differences are its 9x39mm caliber ammunition, bullpup layout and extensive configuration options. This weapon is highly valued by military stalkers due to its ability to kill enemies wearing body armor behind improvised cover at a distance during urban combat, as well as its excellent stopping power.
 
Ammunition:
9x39mm SP-5
9x39mm SP-6
9x39mm PAB-9
under-barrel launcher - VOG-25, VOG-25R

A variant of the OTs-14 “Groza” weapon system chambered for 7.62mm, developed for needs of Russian spetsnaz. The primary advantage of this modification is the ability to use standard 30-round magazines from Kalashnikov-pattern rifles, which simplifies logistics and ammunition standardization.
 
Ammunition:
standard 7.62x39mm
under-barrel launcher - VOG-25, VOG-25R

The GSh-18 is a Russian pistol developed in the early 2000s by the Tula Design Bureau. It is distinguished by its compact size, light weight, and 18-round magazine chambered in 9x19mm. 
 Ammunition:
 standard 9x19mm Parabellum,
 improved 9x19mm JSP-AP.

The HK 53 is a carbine variant of the HK 33KA3 with a shortened barrel that's 221 millimeters long, a extended flash supressor and forend that's similar to HK MP5. No underbarrel grenade launcher or bayonet knife can be installed. This weapon has been manufactured since 1975 and is mainly used by special forces.
 Ammunition:
 standard 5.56x45mm SS109,
 armor-piercing 5.56x45mm AP.

A modified version of the Browning Hi-Power pistol from the first half of the 20th century, which is as reliable, powerful and accurate as the original. Pistols of this series deserve their reputation as one of the best handguns of the 20th century and are in great demand in the Zone.
 Ammunition:
 standard 9x19mm Parabellum,
 improved 9x19mm JSP-AP.
A knife enhanced by the energy of a gravi-artifact, crafted by Cobalt. Features significantly increased stabbing power.
A standard military bayonet-knife. Used in the Zone by army units and ordinary stalkers.
An old and rusty army bayonet knife.
A hunting knife. If you need to take someone out quietly, this knife is the perfect weapon for the job.
The personal knife from a stalker named 'Scrap'. The handle is badly worn, but if you hold it, you'll notice that it fits perfectly in your hand.

After the British army replaced this rifle with the German-made G36, it appeared in large quantities first on the black market and then in the Zone. The L85’s main advantages are a standard 4-x scope and the high accuracy of the first shot. In burst mode, its accuracy decreases greatly, and the main mechanisms of the rifle are not reliable enough.
 Ammunition:
 standard 5.56x45mm SS109,
 armor-piercing 5.56x45mm AP.

An assault rifle developed by the American firm Z-M Weapons, based on the AR-15 platform. The designation "LR-300" stands for "Light Rifle with an effective firing range of up to 300 meters". Compared to the AR-15, it incorporates a shorter gas-operated system, a significantly modified gas-recoil mechanism, and a completely redesigned upper receiver. 
 Ammunition:
 standard 5.56x45mm SS109,
 armor-piercing 5.56x45mm AP.

A semi-automatic rifle developed by Para-Ordnance based on the ZM LR-300. Features an integrated higher-magnification sight. 
Modifications to the rifle's layout, along with refinements to its design and operating mechanism, significantly reduced its weight and improved its accuracy; however, these enhancements came at the cost of a smaller magazine capacity and the loss of automatic fire mode.
 Ammunition:
 standard 5.56x45mm SS109,
 armor-piercing 5.56x45mm AP.

This submachine gun has gained popularity around the world thanks to its reliability, ease of use and accuracy. Over the last few decades the MP5 was in service with special armed forces and police units worldwide. Not surprisingly, having flooded the global black markets, it eventually made its way to the Zone.
 Ammunition:
 standard 9x19mm Parabellum,
 improved 9x19mm JSP-AP.

Due to lower propellant gas pressure, the standard 9x18mm PM cartridge is incompatible with the bolt design of the MP5. This, it seems, is what prompted the technician working on this weapon to adapt it to fire the more powerful JSP-AP and +P+ cartridges instead. A small inscription can be seen on the stock: “Golmar”.
 Ammunition: 
 armor-piercing 9x18mm JSP-AP, 
 improved 9x18mm +P+.

This pistol was developed in the second half of the 20th century for special forces and recon units. Its designation, PB, translates from Russian as "silenced pistol". The front of the pistol's barrel is has an integrated silencer attached to it, while the bolt mechanism is short, which prevents a back-moving spring from being located inside it, and it is therefore situated in the weapon's handle. Although obsolete, the weapon is still effective in the right hands.
 Ammunition:
 standard 9x18mm FMJ,
 armor-piercing 9x18mm JSP-AP, 
 improved 9x18mm +P+.

Designed and manufactured by Izhevsk Machine Engineering Plant in Russia for police and military armament since 1951, this Soviet legacy is the most common pistol in the Zone and is one of the best compact self-defense handguns available. It is small, highly reliable, easy to use and maintain in working order. It also suffers from several drawbacks, including its short range, low firing accuracy and poor stopping power, while also losing out to modern pistols in its class in terms of weight and magazine size.
 Ammunition:
 standard 9x18mm FMJ,
 armor-piercing 9x18mm JSP-AP, 
 improved 9x18mm +P+.

PMM was developed in the early 90s as a more powerful and modern version of the classic Makarov pistol. The pistol features a reinforced frame, a heavier slide, and a 12-round box magazine. The improved chamber design allows for the effective use of 9x18mm +P+, but it is not intended for firing standard 9x18mm PM ammunition. 
 Ammunition: 
 armor-piercing 9x18mm JSP-AP, 
 improved 9x18mm +P+.

This revolver-type grenade launcher uses six rifled front-loading barrels, identical to underbarrel launcher attachments. The drum is also front-loading. The RG-6 is widely used for rapid suppression of enemy positions and, when in the open, attacking defended fixed targets or fighting particularly tough monsters.
 Ammunition:
 VOG-25 grenade
 VOG-25R grenade

This grenade launcher from the 1960s made its way into the Zone from army depots. The RPG-7V is a smoothbore, single-shot, recoilless rocket launcher system with an open-rear tube. It comes with a PGO-7 x2.8 optical scope. Although its huge size and weight make it an unlikely choice for stalkers, given its huge destructive power and ease of use, it has found admirers in the Zone.\n Ammunition:\n OG-7B warhead

The RPK is a light machine gun based on the AKM assault rifle. Adopted into service in 1961, it replaced the Degtyarev light machine gun as a preferred choice in terms of unification with other small arms. At the time of its introduction and for a long time afterward, it was the lightest machine gun in the world. It has proven itself to be a highly effective weapon, compact, simple, and easy to operate, making it used in the Zone primarily by veteran stalkers and rarely by special forces groups.\n Ammunition:\n standard 7.62x39mm.

The RPK-74 is a light machine gun developed to replace the RPK and chambered for the new 5,45x39 mm caliber. It was adopted in 1974, along with the AK-74 assault rifle. In the Zone, it is used by veteran stalkers and special forces soldiers.
 Ammunition:
 standard 5.45x39mm FMJ,
 armor-piercing 5.45x39mm AP.

An export variant of the RPK-74 light machine gun, chambered for the 5.56x45mm cartridge and developed in 1994. It is popular in certain military conflicts beyond the Perimeter, but not within the Zone.
 Ammunition:
 standard 5.56x45mm SS109,
 armor-piercing 5.56x45mm AP.

The SIG Sauer P220 is the only remaining mass produced model of the globally renowned P220 series. This weapon has earned a reputation for its excellent ergonomics and accuracy, and while its magazine is relatively small, it benefits from powerful ammo and a mechanism that functions like a Swiss watch. Some believe the P220 to be the best mass produced .45 ACP caliber handgun there is and it has certainly got a following among experienced stalkers and mercenaries.
 Ammunition:
 standard .45 ACP,
 improved .45 ACP Hydra-Shok.

A relatively new assault rifle chambered for the 5.56x45mm caliber. This weapon is very popular due to its accuracy, soft recoil, and high reliability.
 Ammunition:
 standard 5.56x45mm SS109,
 armor-piercing 5.56x45mm AP.

The SPAS-12 smooth-bore rifle was developed in the late 1970th. This weapon is very reliable and flexibly used. It is however relatively big, expensive and its mechanism is too complex. Probably, this is the best close range gun in the Zone.
 Ammunition:
 12x70 shot,
 12x76 slug,
 12x76 dart.

An army sniper rifle that has been on the market for more than fifty years and has earned its reputation for exceptional reliability and ease of use. The SVD is normally used by armies in countries that are part of the ex-USSR to improve the effective range of its units, but stalkers respect this weapon for its armor-piercing properties, which allows it to penetrate mutant hide and anti-ballistic body armor.
 Ammunition:
 standard 7.62x54R 7N1,
 armor-piercing 7.62x54R AP,
 improved 7.62x54R 7N14.

A modernized version of the SVD sniper rifle that's a compact, bullpup version of it - made to the specifications of Russian special forces units. It allows faster precision fire and is considerably lighter, while its single shot firing accuracy at short and medium range is similar to that of its predecessor. These qualities have earned it the admiration of countless stalkers.
 Ammunition:
 standard 7.62x54R 7N1,
 armor-piercing 7.62x54R AP,
 improved 7.62x54R 7N14.

The OTs-12 "Tiss" is a Russian assault rifle developed by the Tula Central Design Bureau of Sporting and Hunting Weapons (TsKIB SOO) based on the AKS74U. Its key difference is the use of special subsonic 9x39mm cartridges, which necessitated design changes. It is extremely rare in the Zone.
 Ammunition:
 standart 9x39mm PAB-9,
 armor-piercing 9x39mm SP-6,
 sniper 9x39mm SP-5.

The TOZ-34 is a extremely common over-and-under hunting shotgun, offering better protection against mutants than a pistol, thanks to its accuracy and stopping power. It's used mostly by rookies on the outskirts of the Zone. It has been in production since 1964 at the Tula Arms Plant.
 
Ammunition:
12x70 Buckshot,
12x76mm Slug,
12x76mm Dart

Impeccable reliability and durability combined with excellent accuracy are the main noteworthy features of the USP Compact. Its minor drawbacks include its considerable size, relatively high center of gravity and massive bolt, which make it difficult to conceal but do not outweigh the weapon's positive features. The weapon is especially popular with the Zone's veterans.
 Ammunition:
 standard .45 ACP,
 improved .45 ACP Hydra-Shok.

A modified version of the silent Vintorez sniper rifle, this assault rifle was designed as a weapon meant for special forces. The rifle's primary purpose is effective fire against enemies employing modern personal protection equipment without revealing the shooter's location. Thanks to its integrated silencer and 9x39mm caliber round with a heavy subsonic bullet, the weapon's noise and muzzle flash have been reduced to a minimum.
 Ammunition:
 standart 9x39mm PAB-9,
 armor-piercing 9x39mm SP-6,
 sniper 9x39mm SP-5.

A unique Vintorez specimen featuring upgraded optics and a commemorative inscription on the side. Precision has been enhanced through expert fine-tuning, and the magazine has been replaced with a 20-round extended magazine from an AS "Val".
 Ammunition:
 standart 9x39mm PAB-9,
 armor-piercing 9x39mm SP-6,
 sniper 9x39mm SP-5.

The VSS "Vintorez" is a specialized military sniper rifle purpose-built for silent, flashless sniping during special operations where avoiding early detection of the shooter may be critical. It provides high armor-piercing capability and stopping power, as well as being equipped with an integrated sniper and optical scope. Highly rated by many stalkers despite its small magazine.
 Ammunition:
 standart 9x39mm PAB-9,
 armor-piercing 9x39mm SP-6,
 sniper 9x39mm SP-5.

A VSS "Vintorez" that's been modified with a Gravi artifact, improving its ballistic performance. This weapon is an experimental prototype.
 Ammunition:
 standart 9x39mm PAB-9,
 armor-piercing 9x39mm SP-6,
 sniper 9x39mm SP-5.

The Walther P99 is a excellent Western pistol known for its reliability, high capacity magazine and good accuracy, as well as being among the most ergonomic handguns in its class. One of the most widely used pistols in the Zone, both among professionals and rookies who can afford it.
 Ammunition:
 standard 9x19mm Parabellum,
 improved 9x19mm JSP-AP.

The Mossberg Maverick 88 is a Western smoothbore shotgun that is extremely popular around the world due to its great reliability and quick reloading speed. It's particularly valued for its functionality by the Zone's hunters. All of its parts are coated with an anticorrosion compound.
 
Ammunition:
 12x70Buckshot,
12x76mm Slug,
12x76mm Dart
